params.hypothesis: Ischaemia-evidence gate (raises risk). 204 = ReLU(0.247 + 2.593*oldpeak + 0.871*restecg:0 + 1.145*thal:7). Hypothesis: a one-sided ST-depression score that opens above an oldpeak threshold set by two flags (always open with a normal resting ECG and a reversible thallium defect; above z-oldpeak -0.09 with a normal ECG only, -0.33 with a defect only, +0.58 with neither), and then raises the logit with oldpeak, directly (0.143 per unit) and through the blood-pressure gate (a further 0.183 per unit while that gate is open). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 48% (100% of the 44 patients with both flags, 20% of the 75 with neither); corr with oldpeak 0.88; disease rate 66% when active vs 24% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity| oldpeak 1.24 > thal:7 0.55 > restecg:0 0.42. This is the main nonlinear effect: removing it with its downstream effects lowers train AUC 0.942 -> 0.934 (to the linear-core level); an affine replacement recovers 0.938. Supported. Oldpeak and restecg:0 have no direct edge; they act only here. The positive restecg:0 weight (normal ECG raises the score) is counter-intuitive and is reported, not explained.

params.hypothesis: Blood-pressure offset gate on the ischaemia score (raises risk). 290 = ReLU(-0.495 + 1.079*ischaemia_gate - 0.815*trestbps + 0.176*cp:2 + 0.016*cp:3). Hypothesis: passes the ischaemia score on, minus an offset that grows with resting blood pressure; it adds 0.170 per unit to the logit and switches off the age gate. With the ischaemia gate closed it still opens for low resting blood pressure, so within this gate lower resting BP raises risk (0.170*0.815 = 0.139 per SD), partly offsetting trestbps's direct +0.48 edge. cp:2 (atypical angina) nudges it open; cp:3's weight 0.016 is negligible. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 58% (83% with the ischaemia gate open, 35% without); with the ischaemia gate open, active for 100%, 87% and 59% of the low, middle and high resting-BP groups. Disease rate 51% when active vs 35% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity| ischaemia score 0.58 > trestbps 0.45 > cp:2 0.10 > cp:3 0.01. Readout ablation lowers train AUC 0.942 -> 0.939; an affine replacement fits it well (R2 0.97, AUC 0.941), so its nonlinearity matters little. Supported, small. The negative BP term inside a risk-raising gate is reported, not explained.

params.hypothesis: Age gate without ischaemia evidence (raises risk with age, small). 1987 = ReLU(0.203 + 0.875*age - 1.589*bp_offset_gate), read out +0.143. Hypothesis: an extra age term (0.125 per SD of age, on top of age's direct +0.117) that acts only while the BP gate is closed or nearly closed, i.e. for patients without much ischaemia evidence; any opening of the BP gate cancels it (each unit of the BP gate removes 0.227 from the logit through this node until it closes). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): active for 35% (65% when the BP gate is closed, rising with age: 0%, 80%, 100% of the youngest, middle and oldest groups; 14% when the BP gate is open). Disease rate barely differs (43% vs 45%). Mean |sensitivity| BP gate 0.35, age 0.31. Removing it lowers train AUC only 0.942 -> 0.941. Supported, near-negligible.

records.narrative: Root closed form (get_formula force=true); output is sigmoid.
Train-split performance, ablations, linear replacements and SHAP.

params.hypothesis: Root: p = sigmoid(z), z = -0.504 + LINEAR CORE + 0.143*ischaemia_gate + 0.170*bp_offset_gate + 0.143*age_gate_without_ischaemia. LINEAR CORE (19 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.480, sex:0 -1.072, slope:1 -0.855, chol +0.546, cp:1 -0.493, trestbps +0.480, cp:3 -0.440, exang:1 +0.431, thal:3 -0.410, thal:6 -0.384, cp:4 +0.377, slope:3 -0.366, fbs:0 +0.278, thalach -0.207, thal:4 +0.183, slope:2 +0.153, exang:0 +0.149, age +0.117, thal:7 -0.077. Four inputs are unconnected (sex:1, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2; zero-effect entries of this root). Oldpeak, restecg:0 and cp:2 have no direct edge and act only through the chain. COMPOSITION: serial and additive. The three children form a chain, each read out additively into z: ischaemia_gate (oldpeak, normal resting ECG, reversible defect) feeds bp_offset_gate (the ischaemia score minus a resting-BP offset), which in turn switches off age_gate_without_ischaemia (an extra age term for patients without ischaemia evidence). The chain therefore raises risk with ST depression, more steeply where resting BP is low, and adds a small age term where the chain is quiet. Identity nodes identity_290 and identity_1987 carry the chain links (204 -> 290, 290 -> 1987) so that each gate is its own leaf. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.9418, acc 0.872 (compute_performance). Linear core alone AUC 0.934; logit SD 3.14 (core) vs 0.67 (chain). Removing the whole chain (node 204 with downstream) gives 0.934; readout-only ablations: ischaemia 0.940, BP 0.939, age 0.941. Treating all three ReLUs as identities gives 0.936; one least-squares linear fit of the chain on its seven inputs gives 0.937 (R2 0.84); an L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs gives 0.936. Mean |SHAP| (train, all 242): ca 0.144, sex:0 0.110, slope:1 0.100, thal:3 0.048, exang:1 0.047, chol 0.045, cp:4 0.044, cp:3 0.044. Interpretation: close to logistic regression plus one ischaemia correction: ST depression raises risk only above a threshold set by a normal resting ECG and a reversible defect, more so when resting BP is low; age gets a small extra weight when there is no such evidence. Counter-directional signs reported, not explained: restecg:0 positive in the ischaemia gate, trestbps negative in the BP gate, fbs:0 +0.28 directly. Same design as the 10-seed heart-s5 record (generation 37, key 9330: ischaemia gate -> resting-BP gate -> age term), here with three hidden nodes instead of six.
